plan.title: Restore the Flywheel page as a derived view (cut by PAN-3917 FR-13 against operator intent)
plan.author: agent:claude-opus-5

metadata.sizeJustification: One plan on purpose: the issue's acceptance is 'every v1 row has a home' plus 'pan flywheel status and the page agree', and both span the lib, the CLI, the routes, the page, and the skill. Landing the verbs without the page (or the page without the verbs) is exactly the partial restore the operator objected to. Items are small vertical slices with one shared deriver (wi-3) so they still parallelize.

narratives.Problem: PAN-3917 FR-13 deleted the Flywheel dashboard page, its run-record telemetry, and the pause/resume/abort/report/stats verbs, leaving only `pan flywheel start|stop|status` (which answers 'is the tmux session alive') and the pan-flywheel loop skill. The operator did not want the page cut. Today there is no view of what the loop is doing, no home for the auto_pickup_backlog and require_uat_before_merge policies, no pending-auto-merge surface, no state or report file, and the skill lost the pickup-gate vocabulary and the metabolism mission.
narratives.Proposal: Restore every v1 affordance as a derived view. One shared `deriveFlywheelStatus()` in `src/lib/flywheel/` reads the flywheel conversation row, its transcript (the skill prints a parseable `flywheel-tick:` line at the end of every tick), the per-issue pipeline journals, the control-settings policies, and the running order book. The CLI (`pan flywheel status|stats|pause|resume|abort|report|stop|start`), new `/api/flywheel/*` routes, and a restored `/flywheel` page all consume it. The loop maintains `.pan/flywheel/state.md` and writes `.pan/flywheel/report.md` on stop, committed like the backlog sequence. Substrate-bug stats (c1 discovery rate, c2 P0 count, 30d window, trend) are computed on read from the tracker label `substrate-improvement` and merged PRs. No new SQLite table; no run record.
narratives.NonGoals:
- Stats criteria c3–c7 (pass rate, MTTR, intervention, time consistency, flake); their inputs were the deleted telemetry
- Any run record, run id, flywheel_runs table, telemetry service, or POST /api/flywheel/status written by the loop
- Boot reconciliation, Recover button, orphan-test-agent surface, VerifyingOnMain badge, reset/restart-from-plan buttons (same cut commit, separate concerns)
- Moving merge_train_enabled off the Merge train section of Awaiting Merge
- Changing the loop's phases or the pan start launch path
- Re-adding roles/flywheel.md as a launched role prompt (it is cited as source text for the skill only)
- A `.pan/` substrate-bug observation file (D2: the tracker is the source)

autoDecisions.summary: State and report files live at <planHome>/.pan/flywheel/state.md and report.md, not docs/FLYWHEEL-STATE.md.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue's acceptance says the only stores are .pan/ files and the pipeline journal; the loop commits them with commitPlanArtifacts exactly as pan backlog write-sequence commits .pan/backlog.

autoDecisions.summary: Substrate-bug stats are computed on read from tracker issues labeled substrate-improvement plus merged PRs, not from a .pan/ observation file or the pipeline journal.
autoDecisions.rationale: The journal dies with the workspace so it cannot hold a 30-day window; the tracker already holds every substrate bug as a labeled issue, so a second file would drift. The cache's closedWindowDays=14 cannot serve 30 days, so the reader shells gh issue list through an injected, 60s-cached dependency. Only c1 and c2 return; c3–c7 are non-goals.

autoDecisions.summary: The status pane is fed by a parseable `flywheel-tick:` line the skill prints at the end of every tick; parsed by one function used by the CLI and the server.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue asks for status derived from the conversation transcript. Free prose is not parseable; a one-line marker is the smallest contract that keeps the loop free of endpoints and stored records.

autoDecisions.summary: pause = handleConversationStop (session killed, row ended, transcript kept); resume = handleConversationResume then re-send /pan-flywheel; abort = pause without a report; stop = ask the loop to write report.md, wait up to 120s, then pause.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue maps pause/resume to the conversation and report to the loop writing report.md on stop. The existing conversation handlers already do the bookkeeping today's pan flywheel stop skips (markConversationEnded).

autoDecisions.summary: pan flywheel start refuses when a paused flywheel conversation exists unless --fresh.
autoDecisions.rationale: createConversation deletes the row by name, so a plain start over a paused loop would silently drop its conversation; the operator should choose resume or fresh.

autoDecisions.summary: auto_pickup_backlog and require_uat_before_merge get switches in the Flywheel page header; merge_train_enabled stays on the Awaiting Merge page with a read-only chip on the Flywheel page.
autoDecisions.rationale: The issue row says merge_train_enabled lives on the Merge train page and asks for a home for the other two, which currently have no UI at all.

autoDecisions.summary: One shared deriveFlywheelStatus() in src/lib/flywheel/derive-status.ts feeds pan flywheel status, GET /api/flywheel/status, and the page.
autoDecisions.rationale: The acceptance says the CLI and the page must agree, both reading the conversation and the journals; a single deriver makes that true by construction instead of by discipline.

autoDecisions.summary: The flywheel is scoped to the project of its conversation's cwd (process.cwd() of the dashboard when no conversation exists); in-flight issues are that project's workspaces/feature-* directories.
autoDecisions.rationale: v1 read docs/FLYWHEEL-STATE.md from process.cwd(); the loop still runs in the project root; listFeatureWorkspaces already enumerates live feature workspaces and loadIssueStatesForProject derives their state.

autoDecisions.summary: One plan with sizeJustification rather than sibling issues.
autoDecisions.rationale: The no-loss and CLI/page-agreement acceptance criteria span every layer; sibling issues would serialize behind the deriver anyway and leave a partial restore in between.
